question_html: AAR Ltd. is formed to take over the assets and liabilities of ABC Ltd., which is then dissolved. This is an example of:
answer_html: Answer: (C) External reconstruction — a new company (AAR Ltd.) is formed specifically to take over a single existing company (ABC Ltd.), which is dissolved; this is distinct from Absorption (an existing company takes over another) and from Amalgamation (two or more existing companies combine).
topic_text: Amalgamation of Companies (2): External reconstruction vs. absorption vs. amalgamation - distinguishing definitions

question_html: Amalgamation adjustment reserve is opened in the books of the amalgamated company to incorporate:

options.A: Non-current assets of the amalgamating company
options.B: Non-Statutory reserves of the amalgamating company
options.C: Statutory reserves of the amalgamating company
options.D: General reserves of the amalgamating company

answer_html: Answer: (C) Statutory reserves of the amalgamating company.
